claim_snapshot.title: The Compound Interest of Small Publishing Habits

datasheet.best_title: The Compound Interest of Small Publishing Habits
datasheet.core_claim: Small, repeated publishing habits compound into durable creative advantage.
datasheet.short_joke: No joke—the point works better straight.

beats: You assume the big launch is what grows a channel, yet the accounts that last are built on small weekly publishing habits that nobody notices at first.
The root issue is that attention compounds: each small piece teaches you something, seeds search surface, and lowers the cost of the next piece. Skipping weeks resets the curve.
Reframe publishing not as performance but as deposits. A modest piece shipped on schedule beats a perfect piece shipped never, because the interest accrues on consistency, not on peaks.
Before chasing the next big idea, fix the cadence. Choose a sustainable weekly slot, define a minimum publishable unit, and protect it. Let the compounding do the dramatic work.
